Security Alert: Critical Compromise Detected

Analysis Summary:
I've identified a highly suspicious sequence of events indicating an active compromise of the LAB-PC-07 workstation. The activity follows a classic attack pattern and involves privileged account takeover and malware execution.

Critical Findings:

Privileged Account Takeover (CRITICAL)

04:18:22: Password changed for local Administrator account from 127..0.0.1 (local system).
04:19:05: Successful Administrator login from 192.168.1.45 immediately after the password change.
Pattern: Password reset → successful privileged access within 43 seconds. This indicates credential compromise.

Malware Execution (CRITICAL)

04:21:18: Process PWNED_BY_OwlSec.exe launched by Administrator from:
C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\PWNED_BY_OwlSec.exe.
Key Indicators:
Malicious filename (PWNED indicates attacker acknowledgment).
Execution path suggests manual placement (not system/application directory).
High-severity event directly following privileged access.

Off-Hours Activity
All events occurred between 04:18-04:23 AM (non-business hours), increasing suspicion.

Anomalous Source IPs

Password change from 127.0.0.1 (local) but login from 192.168.1.45 (internal
